overview: Tula was a major early Postclassic city with planned neighborhoods and far-reaching exchange. Scholars debate how its political power relates to later stories of Toltec greatness.

items.text: Irrigated maize fields and canals supported the local economy.
Residential compounds and a street grid suggest coordinated urban planning. Households shared courtyards for daily and ritual activities.
Plumbate pottery found at Tula links the city with production in Chiapas and Guatemala. Imported goods are evidence of connections, not automatic proof of conquest.
Carved human-shaped columns supported the roof of a temple on Pyramid B. Traces of paint show that the stone architecture was once colored.
Pohl places the site approximately 800-1150 CE. The causes of Toltec decline remain uncertain, and no single conquering successor is established here.
